data.heading: Five ways to support a local cause (besides donating)
data.body:
Money matters to every nonprofit, but it's not the only way to help. Here are five other ways to make a difference.

  • Volunteer your time, even for a few hours a month.
  • Share your skills, such as design, accounting, writing or IT.
  • Spread the word by sharing posts and telling friends.
  • Organize a collection at your workplace, school or club.
  • Ask your employer about matching gifts or team volunteering days.

Whatever you choose, ask the organization what would help most right now. Needs change through the year, and a quick question makes sure your time goes where it counts.

And if you do decide to give money, regular small gifts can help a charity plan ahead.

Small acts add up. A share on social media can reach someone who becomes a regular volunteer or supporter.

If you'd like to get involved with [Your Organization Name], get in touch. We'd love to hear from you.

data.heading: What to expect on your first volunteer day
data.body:
Volunteering for the first time can feel a little nerve-wracking. Here's what usually happens, so you know what to expect.

When you arrive, someone from our team will welcome you, show you around and introduce you to other volunteers.

We'll explain your role and any safety information. Please ask questions. There's no such thing as a silly one.

You'll usually work alongside someone experienced on your first day, so you're never left on your own.

If you have any access needs, or there's anything we should know to help you feel comfortable, tell us before you come. We'll do our best to make it work.

Wear comfortable clothes and bring water. We'll tell you in advance if you need anything else.

At the end, we'll ask how it went and talk about when you might like to come back.

Thank you for giving your time. Volunteers are at the heart of everything [Your Organization Name] does.
